object_context: Necessary trace-legitimacy filter for any successful exact compact-resolvent Hilbert–Pólya realization of the Riemann zeros: assuming a self-adjoint operator H has discrete spectrum whose nonzero eigenvalues, with the declared one-sided or two-sided convention and exact algebraic multiplicities, match all nontrivial zeta-zero ordinates up to a finite perturbation, determine the sharp Schatten threshold of (I+H^2)^(-alpha/2) from zero counting alone. This atom is a no-go/filter, not a construction of H and not an RH proof.
structural_coordinates: exact RH binding is the canonical statement that every nontrivial zero rho of zeta has Re(rho)=1/2; this atom supplies only a necessary condition on a hypothetical exact spectral realization

H must be densely defined self-adjoint on a specified Hilbert space; compact resolvent (or an explicitly equivalent purely discrete finite-multiplicity spectral hypothesis) is assumed only for the Schatten calculation

spectral completeness and multiplicity matching are load-bearing: the eigenvalue counting function must agree with the Riemann zero counting function up to a fixed finite error and an explicitly declared factor from +/- duplication
von Mangoldt zero counting gives N(T)=T/(2*pi)*log(T/(2*pi))-T/(2*pi)+O(log T), hence N(T) is asymptotic to (T/(2*pi))*log T
for A_alpha=(I+H^2)^(-alpha/2), membership A_alpha in S_p is equivalent to summability of (1+lambda_n^2)^(-alpha*p/2) over spectral multiplicity
ordinary trace legitimacy is distinct from distributional, zeta-regularized, heat-kernel, relative, or other renormalized trace identities
the counting asymptotic alone carries no prime-side weights, phases, test-function class, or explicit-formula normalization, so prime matching cannot be inferred
finite-zero agreement and random-matrix/GUE statistics are calibration only and cannot establish completeness, multiplicity, self-adjointness, or trace legitimacy
finite spectral perturbations and the choice of one-sided versus +/- symmetric enumeration alter only finitely many terms or a constant factor and therefore do not alter the Schatten threshold
equivalent_formulations: write dN for the zero-counting Stieltjes measure and determine convergence of integral_1^infinity (1+t^2)^(-alpha*p/2) dN(t)
using N(T) asymptotic T log T, determine the critical exponent q for sum_n (1+lambda_n^2)^(-q/2)
falsify any compact-resolvent HP route whose proposed ordinary trace requires (H-i)^(-1) or (I+H^2)^(-1/2) to be trace class
separate the admissible stronger-smoothing/regularized trace routes from the inadmissible first-order ordinary-trace route without claiming a spectral construction
solved_analogues: Toy counting law N_toy(T)=floor(T log(e+T)): direct integral comparison gives sum (1+lambda_n^2)^(-q/2)<infinity exactly for q>1, exhibiting the same threshold without arithmetic content.

For a positive sequence with N(T) asymptotic C*T^d, Stieltjes integration gives the familiar counting-to-Schatten threshold q>d; RH zero counting behaves like spectral dimension one with an extra logarithm, so the endpoint q=1 still diverges.
near_solved_analogues: Classical Weyl-law arguments convert eigenvalue counting growth into heat-trace and resolvent-power summability, but they do not identify arithmetic prime weights.

Spectral-triple summability uses singular-value growth to define a metric dimension; the RH counting law suggests a weak-L1 endpoint rather than trace class, but no noncommutative-geometric construction is assumed here.

method_transfers.method: transfer counting growth to Schatten membership by Stieltjes summation (or dyadic shell comparison) of a monotone spectral weight
shared_structure: Schatten membership reduces to singular-value p-summability through functional calculus
required_assumptions: H is self-adjoint so the Borel functional calculus defines (I+H^2)^(-alpha/2)
the target spectrum is complete with finite multiplicities under a fixed enumeration convention
the counting asymptotic is applied to the same multiset whose singular values enter the Schatten sum
disanalogies: the Riemann counting law has a T log T factor rather than a pure power Weyl law

method_transfers.repair_question: Can a proposed exact HP model satisfy its desired trace formula using smoothing strictly stronger than first order, or a rigorously defined regularized/distributional trace, without silently invoking an ordinary trace that the zero count forbids?

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: For compact geometric spectral problems, eigenvalue counting controls which inverse powers of an operator are trace class; the endpoint identifies an effective spectral dimension and may require weak or regularized traces.

endpoint divergence is a structural obstruction rather than a finite-size numerical defect
stronger smoothing can restore ordinary trace class

inverse elliptic operator -> (I+H^2)^(-1/2) or resolvent-scale smoothing

cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before searching for a trace formula, infer the cheapest summability class forced by the target counting law and reject operator families whose claimed ordinary trace requires more summability than the target can have.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For RH-SPEC-003, prove the threshold directly from von Mangoldt counting and exhibit explicit exemptions (higher smoothing and regularized/distributional traces); do not infer any RH conclusion.
